## Findings
- claim-1: The paper records the minimality of both Theorem \(5.4\) generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) as conjectural and reports finite computer verification for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1497-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: For a graded connected algebra and a graded module bounded below, homogeneous generators are equivalent to generators of \(M/\Lambda_+M\); inclusion-minimal generating families correspond to inclusion-minimal spanning families of that quotient. [source-2@L1520-L1533|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Minimality does not imply that indecomposables are free of the same rank, even for a torsion-free underlying abelian module. Let \(R=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(M=(2,x)\subset R\). Then \(\{2,x\}\) is an inclusion-minimal homogeneous \(R\)-generating family, \(M\) is torsion-free over \(\mathbb Z\), and \[ M/R_+M=M/xM\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2. \]
- claim-4: Minimality also does not determine rational rank. For \(M=R=\mathbb Z[x]\), the homogeneous family \(\{2,3\}\) is inclusion-minimal and generates \(R\), but \[ M/R_+M=R/xR\cong\mathbb Z, \] of rank \(1\), although the family has cardinality \(2\).
- claim-5: If \(M\) is a finite-rank free abelian group and \(N\subseteq M\), then \[ M/N\cong\mathbb Z^N \] holds if and only if \(N\) is saturated in \(M\) and \[ \dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl((M\otimes\mathbb Q)/(N\otimes\mathbb Q)\bigr)=N. \]
- claim-6: For the proposed \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), a direct proof must separately establish saturation of \(\Lambda_+J_v\) and the indicated rational dimension; minimality alone cannot provide either conclusion.
## Strategy
Let \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), \(J=J_v\subset A\), and \(N=A_+J\). Since the graded quotient map \(\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow A\) maps \(\Lambda_+\) onto \(A_+\),
\[
\operatorname{im}(\Lambda_+J)=A_+J=N.
\]

Conditional on the interval Schur presentation
\[
J=\bigoplus_{\alpha\subseteq\lambda\subseteq\beta}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda,
\]
\(J\) is finite free abelian and graded. Thus
\[
J/N=\bigoplus_d J_d/N_d.
\]
For each degree \(d\), form the complete integral Pieri matrix \(P_d\), with columns the Schur basis of \(J_d\) and rows all products \(h_t\bar s_\lambda\) whose degree is \(d\), for a generating set of \(A_+\). Its row lattice is \(N_d\).

Smith normal form gives
\[
J_d/N_d\cong \mathbb Z^{\,\nullity(P_d)}
 \oplus\bigoplus_{\delta\in\operatorname{SNF}(P_d),\,\delta>1}\mathbb Z/\delta.
\]
Hence, for an integer \(m\),
\[
J/N\cong\mathbb Z^m
\]
iff every nonzero Smith invariant of every complete \(P_d\) equals \(1\), and
\[
\sum_d\nullity(P_d)=m.
\]
This is an exact finite reduction whenever the Schur interval and complete Pieri rows are established.

There is also a logical obstruction to deriving this result from minimality. With \(R=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(R_+=(x)\), and \(M=(2,x)\),
\[
M/xM=(2,x)/(2x,x^2)\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2,
\]
although \(\{2,x\}\) is inclusion-minimal and \(M\) is torsion-free. Likewise \(\{2,3\}\) is an inclusion-minimal generating family of \(R\), whereas
\[
R/xR\cong\mathbb Z
\]
has rank \(1\). Thus irredundancy neither proves saturation nor determines rational rank.

## Gaps
The general project target remains unresolved: no uniform proof establishes that all complete Pieri relation lattices \(N_d\) are saturated, nor that their nullities sum to \(\binom{a+b}{a}\).

The 2024 theorem recorded in the project context proves minimality only for one of the two source families; it does not state the stronger integral indecomposables conclusion. Minimality therefore cannot fill either gap.

For a uniform matrix proof, one must also establish a complete interval-Schur presentation for the relevant \(J_v\) and verify that the chosen Pieri rows generate all of \(A_+J_v\), not merely a sublattice.

## Next
Prove a uniform saturation statement for the complete degreewise Pieri matrices, for example by explicit unimodular elimination or a combinatorial unitriangular minor. Separately compute the rational nullity sum. Combining those two results through the criterion above would prove the integral indecomposables statement.
